And that was the beginning of suspicion.

Why did I hate these people at a level that seemed animal? Why did it frustrate and anger me when I saw Christians wary of profanity. Why did it sicken me when I saw Christians abstain from pre-marital sex? Why did it fill me with discontent when I saw Christians respond with grace in situations of social pressure and berating? Why did their lives seem 'complete' in a way undefineable? Because they had a piece of the human experience that I lacked. They had a framework for life.

They had an explanation not only for the existence of things, but more importantly a description of the depth, mystery, and depravity of the human heart and soul. Christians are not perfect people. They do not follow their bible 100%, because to do so is impossible, and was done by one man, Jesus. This makes them hypocrites; holders of the perfect word of God but imperfect people.

If I haven't sickened your godless heart yet, and I mean that in the kindest way possible, I encourage you to stop dismissing Christianity. I'm not asking you to run down to the local church and start rolling around on the floor speaking in tongues. I ask you only for your disinterested consideration and common human decency. Christianity has more to offer this world than any political ideology, any economic system, any philosophy, because it addresses the indescribably complex and mysterious existence of the hole in the soul of human beings that says constantly 'I'm not good enough'.

I love my religion. I love my God, and I even now sometimes love my life, which for me is a massive achievement in personal growth. When I consider the person I used to be, and even so now, I can attribute my happiness, my comfort, my growth, my safety, my friendships and all good things to nothing other than the grace of God.

I hope this post has made you curious or uncomfortable.
